elements.source: Presentations 1-6: asymptomatic, macrohematuria, nephrotic syndrome, nephritic syndrome (acute GN), RPGN, CKD (chronic GN).
Note: CKD of vascular disease ischemic nephropathy; CKD of glomerular disease CKD CGN.
Asymptomatic urine abnormalities (m/c presentation): proteinuria >500 mg/24 hrs + microhematuria >=3 RBC/HPF; proteinuria alone >1 g/24 hrs.
Macrohematuria: on urine analysis; 40/5/1 rule (>=40 dysmorphic, >=5 acanthocytes, 1 RBC cast) + significant proteinuria -> biopsy.
Criteria: 1 nephrotic range proteinuria; 2 hypoalbuminemia <3 g/dl; 3 edema extravascular; adults 1+2+3; children 1+2 or 3.
Note: hyperlipidemia, lipiduria were previously part of diagnostic criteria.
Nephrotic range proteinuria - total protein: adults >3500 mg/24 hrs; children >50 mg/kg/day.

pages.traversal: PCR adult >=3000 / children >=2000 mg/g; not diagnostic; also seen in (diabetes m/c, 2 degree FSGS, amyloidosis) Rx ACEi/ARB; 'Childhood Nephrotic Syndrome': proteinuria + hypoalbuminemia + edema -> nephrotic range / extravascular > intravascular; HYPOALBUMINEMIA two bullets; Sign: Muehrcke's line photo; EDEMA pathophysiology: underfill > overfill; underfill chain.

elements.source: Urine PCR: adult >=3000 mg/g; children >=2000 mg/g; not diagnostic of nephrotic syndrome.
Also seen in: diabetes (m/c), 2 degree FSGS, amyloidosis - Rx: ACE inhibitors, ARB.
Childhood NS: proteinuria + hypoalbuminemia + edema; nephrotic range; extravascular > intravascular.
HYPOALBUMINEMIA: urinary loss of albumin; down compensation by liver.
Sign: white transverse line - Muehrcke's line.
EDEMA pathophysiology: underfill theory > overfill theory.

Underfill: hypoalbuminemia -> loss of capillary oncotic pressure -> fluid to interstitium -> periorbital puffiness, pedal edema (extravascular) / down effective circulatory volume -> 2 degree RAS -> aldosterone -> Na+, water retention (intravascular).

pages.traversal: Overfill theory (nephritic): 1 beta hemolytic streptococci -> plasmin -> ENaC -> 1 degree RAS -> Na+/water retention; 2 ANP resistance; management boxes MCD / FSGS / MN, IgA rare; Risk of thrombosis: albumin <2 g/dl, causes, correction of albumin; Edema manifestation: ascites / pleural effusion / pericardial effusion.

elements.source: Overfill theory: beta hemolytic streptococci -> releases plasmin -> activates ENaC -> 1 degree RAS activation -> retention of Na+, water (intravascular edema).
2. ANP resistance.
Management boxes: MCD 85-90%, steroid responsive (95%), no role of biopsy; FSGS genetic form unresponsive to steroid -> renal transplantation; MN, IgA rare.
Risk of thrombosis: serum albumin <2 g/dl -> renal vessel thrombosis, CVT, DVT.
Causes: loss of antithrombin III in urine; loss of protein C, S in urine; up platelet aggregation; up fibrinogen; down plasminogen.
Correction of albumin (to >2 g/dL): 20% albumin 20 g/100 ml; dose 0.5 g/kg; FFP, egg white can also be used.
Edema manifestation: ascites (moderate to severe) Rx tapping, m/c death pneumococcal peritonitis; pleural effusion (mild); pericardial effusion (rare) disproportional dyspnoea Ix echo.

pages.traversal: Treatment for edema four bullets; Daily monitoring three bullets; Note: features against MCD; Steroid regimen -> taper -> stop -> remission 90-95% (two bullets) / SRNS 5-10%; Hyperlipidemia three bullets; pathogenesis four bullets; associated features; xanthelasma photo.

elements.source: Treatment for edema: salt <2 g/day; protein 1 g/kg/day; albumin, FFP; diuretics avoided - only if IVC non-collapsible; precipitates pre-renal AKI.
Daily monitoring: weight; urine routine examination; urine PCR.
Note - features against MCD: RBC casts in urine; hypertension; renal failure.
Steroid: oral prednisolone 2 mg/kg/day (or) 60 mg/m2/day x 6 wks; max 80 mg/day; taper x 6 weeks; stop.
Remission 90-95%: urine albumin nil/trace x 3 consecutive days; urine PCR <200 mg/g; SRNS 5-10%.
Hyperlipidemia: resolves with steroid therapy; no risk of atherosclerosis; no role for statin.
Pathogenesis: loss of HDL in urine; up lipoprotein lipase up TG; down LCAT down HDL; up VLDL, LDL synthesis by liver.
Associated features: xanthoma, xanthelasma (photo).

pages.traversal: SRNS: proteinuria despite full dose steroid 4 wk -> biopsy (1st indication in child) -> genetic FSGS (podocin) Rx transplant / MCD treatment CNI (DOC) duration, max; tacrolimus dose and S/E; cyclosporine S/E; Relapse flowchart 25/25/50; steroid sparing drugs; relapse after intermission; SDNS definition; treatment MMF, rituximab.

elements.source: SRNS: proteinuria despite full dose of steroid for 4 wk -> biopsy (1st indication in child).
Genetic form of FSGS (podocin mutation) -> Rx renal transplantation.
MCD treatment: calcineurin inhibitors (DOC) duration 6 months, max 2 yrs; tacrolimus 0.1 mg/kg/day S/E neuropathy, DM, alopecia; cyclosporine S/E hirsutism, gingival hyperplasia.
Relapse: proteinuria after 1 month of steroid; 25% no further relapse (very quick remission); 25% infrequent relapse; 50% FRNS.
Infrequent relapse -> steroid -> taper over 4 wks during remission.
FRNS: >=2 relapse within 6 months; >=4 relapse within 1 year; steroid sparing drug: oral cyclophosphamide 2 mg/kg/day x 12 wks + steroid x 2 wks; oral levamisole.
Relapse: proteinuria reappears after 1 month of intermission.
SDNS: >=2 consecutive relapses during tapering (or) within 14 days after stopping steroid; treatment MMF 1200 mg/m2/day; rituximab 375 mg/m2/day x 4 doses.

elements.source: Proteinuria: urine PCR >=3000 mg/d; edema; hypoalbuminemia.
Causes: membranous nephropathy (m/c); FSGS; MCD (15%); IgA; MPGN, 2 degree amyloidosis - rare.
Management: 1 biopsy; 2 rule out 2 degree causes (eg paraneoplastic syndrome).
Treatment: steroid 1 mg/kg/d x 4 months -> no response -> SRNS (m/c FSGS).
Note: maltese crosses in polarized light; oval fat bodies -> seen in Fabry's disease.
